# kayjs-cms

> A CMS for kay sites: content edited on the page it renders, and collection screens.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- The app writes no marker: in edit mode kay marks each element rendering an entry's field itself, `data-kay-field="<collection>:<slug>[@<locale>]:<path>"`, each segment URI-encoded, the path dotted with list indexes (`sections.1.heading`). A field in an attribute is `data-kay-field-<attribute>`, a field sharing its element's text sits between `<!--kay-field …-->` and `<!--/kay-field-->`, and a Markdown body is `data-kay-body="<collection>:<slug>"` or a `kay-body` comment pair.
- The body's path is the `BODY` symbol, never a string, so a data field named `body` stays a data field.
- Outside edit mode the page is unchanged and the editor is not rendered.
- Draft rendering happens on the server: the editor sends the changed entries, kay renders the page with them and swaps it in, islands kept.
- Every change goes through one API, `POST` and `DELETE /api/cms/entries/:collection/:slug` and `POST …/:slug/publish`, from the sidebar and from the screens alike. kay validates the data against the schema and names the file; kay writes nothing, the configured `files` saver does.
- An `imageField()` or `fileField()` holds a path the site serves. A file dropped or picked on it goes to `POST /api/cms/files/:collection`, `uploads.maxSize` at most (20 MB by default), an empty file refused 400, a bigger one 413, which stores it public through kay's `files.put` in a folder named for the collection, and the field keeps `files.url(key)`, `/_kay/files/<key>`; a typed path works as well, so a page renders either with `img(src={entry.data.photo})`. An image pasted or dropped into a Markdown body, the entry's or a `markdown` field's, goes to the same endpoint and is embedded as `![](path)` where the cursor is; the pickers offer only the types `uploads` takes (images for an image field) and `GET /api/cms/files/rules` tells the editor them with the size limit, so a dropped file they miss, or one over the size, is toasted with its type or size and a refused upload leaves the text as it was. Replacing or removing a file leaves the old upload stored: the unused-uploads screen at `<prefix>/uploads` lists the uploads directly in a collection's folder that no entry mentions, in any collection, locale, draft or loaded collection, each with the image variants it would take with it, and deletes only the ones you confirm, and only with a `guard`. Uploads under a day old, or that the storage dates not at all, are held back: a save the site has not rebuilt from, another server's save or an unsaved form may use them. A URL written by hand in a page, a file of the repository outside the collections or an older revision a revert brings back is not seen either, so check each upload before you confirm; the screen lists nothing while a collection or entry cannot be read, or the storage cannot list its files. `POST /api/cms/files/unused/delete` takes `{ keys }` and deletes those still unused, answering `{ deleted, kept }`, or 409 while the entries cannot be read.
- The app imports kayjs-ui's theme. The screens and the editor render their own `Toaster` and `TooltipHost`, which render nothing while the app's are mounted; kayjs-ui is a peer dependency, so both resolve the one copy that guard lives in.
- The screens are closed without a `guard`: kayjs-cms has no users of its own.
- Edit mode is kay's preview mode, so the app sets `preview.secret`. Edit mode alone reads entries through the API; once there is a guard, every save, publish, delete and upload needs it too, since an edit cookie or link is tied to no user.

## Setup

`kay add cms` installs the packages and adds `cms()` to `extensions`.

```ts
import { cms, forgejo } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-cms'
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({ extensions: [cms({ guard: { load: async () => (await import('./src/auth')).auth.guard({ require: 'editor' }) }, files: forgejo({ url, repo: 'me/site', token }) })] })
```

- `cms({ prefix, guard, files, uploads, rawHtml, author })`: `prefix` is where the screens live (`/admin`), `guard` who may use them and the API, as `{ load }` returning the guard, which runs on the first request so `kay.config.ts` imports nothing of the app's auth or database, or the built guard itself, which does import it, `files` where a folder entry's file goes, `workingTree()` by default, which a production server refuses to boot with unless named, as the next deploy would drop its saves. `uploads` lists the types a file field takes, exact or `image/*`, PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, AVIF and PDF by default, the type read off the file name's extension as kay's storage serves it; another is answered 415. `uploads: { types, maxSize }` also sets the most an upload may weigh, bytes or `'50mb'` as kay's `budget` takes them, 20 MB by default; the upload route reads that much whatever the app's `bodyLimit`, so nothing else is raised, and a `maxSize` that is zero, negative or fractional in bytes throws as `kay.config.ts` loads. A save whose body renders HTML that would run as the site or cover it, every tag and attribute kay's sanitizer drops (a `<script>`, an `<svg>`, a `<form>` or an input, an `on*`, `style` or `formaction` attribute), a `javascript:` URL in any URL attribute, or a tag left open or wrapped around a component, read off the HTML kay renders as a browser tokenizes it, is refused with an issue on the body, unless `rawHtml` lists its collection; the collection's own components, HTML in code and Markdown's task lists pass, and publishing keeps the stored body unchecked. `author` names who a save is committed as, from the guard's context, so only with a `guard`: `author: async ({ locals }) => { const user = await locals.auth.user(); return user && { name: user.name, email: user.email } }`.
- `forgejo({ url, repo, branch?, token, timeout?, fetch? })`: commits each file through Forgejo's contents API, reading the file's current sha first. Throws `ForgeError` with Forgejo's `status` and message, its first 200 characters (the log gets the rest), 504 when the save, its requests together, takes over `timeout` ms (15,000; the read naming the version after a conflict has its own), or 502 naming why the forge could not be reached; one failing once the commit was sent says it may still have gone through. The editor sees it as the save's issue, the log getting the whole error. Forgejo refusing the commit's sha (409, or 422 naming the sha) throws `SaveConflict`.
- A save or a delete names the version of the file the editor opened, its git blob sha (`fileVersion(text)`): a saver finding the file at another, as after another editor's save, or one's own before the site rebuilt from it, throws `SaveConflict` with the version it found as `current`. The editor keeps the refusal shown while the editor types, and its Keep my edits button takes that version as the one the edits were made from, so the next save writes them over it; nothing else is lost. A new entry must not exist yet. An app's own `FileSaver` checks `change.base` the same way, `null` meaning the file must not exist and `undefined` writing whatever is there; `workingTree()` checks and writes one save of a file at a time.
- The API refuses a save or a delete naming no version for a folder entry the server holds, as from an editor older than the server, logging it: reloading the page loads the editor that names it. A delete from the entry list names the version the list showed, and one from the editor after Keep my edits over a file deleted and made again since names none, so it is refused with a message telling the editor to reload rather than that it is older. Edits kept over a file deleted meanwhile are written as a new entry, refused if the file was made since.
- A file whose blob sha is not what `fileVersion` gives conflicts on every save: a repository checked out with CRLF line endings the server converts, or one using SHA-256 object names.
- Saving again while a save is on its way waits for it, then saves the edits typed meanwhile once.
- `workingTree()`: writes or deletes the file in place, for `kay dev`, or a server whose files outlive a deploy.
- A folder collection's source files ship with the server: kay throws for a folder missing from the build, and for one outside the repository. Slugs follow kay's rules, and a file that does not parse lists as broken, its form opening empty to write over it, a Markdown file keeping its body. A collection whose loader throws is listed as one that cannot be read, its error going to the server's log rather than the screens, which may name a database or its credentials.

## Screens

- `<prefix>`: each collection with its entry count.
- `<prefix>/collections/<collection>`: its entries, 50 a page, titled by their first one-line text field, searched by title and slug (`?q=`), with Publish for a draft, Edit on page for an entry kay knows the page of, and Delete.
- `<prefix>/collections/<collection>/<slug>` (`?locale=`): the entry's form, with Save, Reset, Publish, Delete and Edit on page.
- `<prefix>/new/<collection>` (`?locale=`): a new entry, its slug typed, and in a localized collection its locale, one the site serves.
- `<prefix>/uploads`: the unused uploads, each with its variants and a Delete that asks first; ticked rows are deleted together, the content read once for all.
- `<prefix>/page?path=`: opens the page in edit mode.

## API

- `fieldsOf(schema)`: the form fields of a collection's JSON Schema, in order, each `{ key, label, required, hint, kind }`. Kinds: `text`, `textarea` (a string whose `maxLength` is over 120), `markdown`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `image`, `file`, `json` (any shape without a control), `select` (an enum or a union of literals, with `options`), `reference` (with `collection`), `list` (with `item`) and `group` (with `fields`). kay's `x-kay: { kind }` hint wins over the type. A nullable field is optional.
- `emptyValue(field)`: what a new list item starts as.
- `parseMarker(value, body?)`, `formatMarker(marker)`, `entryKey(ref)`: read and write kay's markers.
- `fieldsAt(node)`: the fields rendered at a node, innermost first.
- `createDrafts({ show, delay })`: the unsaved edits of a page's entries. `open(entry, version?)`, `version(ref)`, `value(ref, path)`, `set(ref, path, value)`, `changed(ref)`, `reset(ref)`, `markSaved(ref, sent, version?)` (what was sent becomes the saved state, an edit typed meanwhile staying unsaved), `refuse(ref, refusal)`, `refusal(ref)` and `keepEdits(ref)` (why a save was refused as a whole, kept until the entry saves or resets, and taking a conflict's version), `issues(ref, path?)`, `failure()` and `rendering()`. Each change renders the page with every changed entry once typing pauses `delay` ms (150), keeping only the latest render's issues.
- `valueAt(data, path)`, `withValueAt(data, path, value)`, `joinPath(parent, key)`: field paths.

## Dev tool

- `cms()` adds a CMS tab to the dev tool under `kay dev`, with nothing to add in the app: whether the visitor is in edit mode, a button into it for the page shown (through the screens' `page` route, so the guard decides) and one out of it (the `preview/exit` route). It reads `/_kay/cms`, a route mounted under `kay dev` alone.
